rationale: Form of unclear etymology in editor's restored opening line. Possibly Greek-derived adjective/verb πρότερος / Latin prior 'former, earlier' adopted into Coptic with verbalizing ⲣ̄-. Alternative analyses: (a) ⲡⲣ̄-ⲓⲱⲣ as 'the doer of ⲓⲱⲣ' with unidentified ⲓⲱⲣ; (b) corruption of πρωΐ-stem 'early.' Function in context (relative-clause attribute introducing the chronologically-prior moment of Christ's coming) supports temporal/sequential 'prior/foremost.' Confidence low; flag for parallels.

Untranslated lexeme in line 14 introducing a locative phrase: ϩⲓ ⲕⲛ̄ϩⲉ ⲟⲩⲧⲱⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲁⲩⲧ = 'at the X of a mountain of the dead.' Possible analyses: (a) Lyc compound ⲕⲟⲩⲛ-ϩⲉ 'bosom-place'; (b) variant of ⲕⲣⲟ 'edge, shore' (with sound-shift); (c) place-name. The construction ϩⲓ + locative-noun supports 'side, edge, bosom' as the structural sense. Confidence low.

Compound noun-phrase ⲧⲱⲟⲩ 'mountain' + 'of-the-dead-ones.' Apparent Manichaean cosmographic-narrative locus where Christ stood after the temptation and Simon's house. May be: (a) Mount of Olives (with reference to dead/sepulchres), (b) Calvary/Golgotha, (c) a primordial Mountain-of-the-Dead in Manichaean typology. Translation literal pending parallels.

Greek loanword πεντηκοστή 'fiftieth (day).' Manichaean ecclesiastical term for the fifty-day Lent/fast-period. Glossed by the apostle himself in the text: 'they call them pentecost' since the count is fifty. Capitalized as proper liturgical name.

Coptic ⲙⲉⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'sign, mark, manner.' Already attested in accumulated vocabulary; reaffirmed here in technical typological register: ⲁⲡⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ = 'unto the type of the Second Man.' The fifty-day Pentecost-fast functions as the ⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ (type) of the Second Man (Christ as Second Adam) revealed in the Church.

Per glossary ⲡⲩⲟ̄ⲓⲧ = 'the foremost' (Lyc reflex of ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄). Applied here as epithet of Simon — most plausibly identifying Simon Peter as 'the foremost' of the disciples. Distinct from Simon Iscariot or Simon the Leper of Gospel narratives. Confirms Manichaean Christological ordering of apostolic primacy.

proposed_english: the First Man / the Second Man
rationale: Pauline-Manichaean Christological pair (1 Cor 15:45-47): the First Man (Adam / Primal Man) and the Second Man (Christ / Second Adam). Already in glossary as ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'First Man' (cosmogonic) and the Second Living Man (apostolic). Here the kephalaion's typology maps the catechumens' fifty days to the First-Man mystery and the elect's fifty days to the Second-Man type.
